items.title: Army kicks off ‘manufacturing rodeo’ with focus on small drones

items.title: These Are The Weapons Ukraine Used To Drop The Kerch Bridge

items.title: Biodata, AI and the future of command: Getting it right

items.title: Keeping America Out: Revisiting China’s Deterrence Strategy for Taiwan
items.snippet: In 2025, Joel Wuthnow wrote “How China Could Counter U.S. Intervention in War Over Taiwan,” arguing that Beijing’s best option might be to deter Washington from coming to Taiwan’s aid by raising the risks to the U.S. homeland. A year and a half later, we asked him to revisit that argument.Image: Lance Cpl. Victor Gurro
items.summary: The article revisits arguments about how China might deter U.S. intervention in a war over Taiwan, including by raising risks to the U.S. homeland.
items.why: The discussion concerns deterrence strategy and the geographic reach of risks in a Taiwan contingency.

items.title: Russia reportedly wants Finland to leave NATO as part of Ukraine deal. History, geography explain why.
items.snippet: Finland’s historical experience with Russia, shaped by centuries of territorial disputes, war and changing borders, is fundamentally different from that of other nations, for instance, Sweden, which joined NATO only a year after Helsinki did.
items.summary: The report links Finland’s historical experience with Russia and territorial disputes to its distinct position in NATO discussions.
items.why: Finland’s geography and history shape how regional security issues are understood.

analysis.headline: Industrial Vulnerability Advisories Put Inventory in Focus
paragraphs: Today’s top stories are concentrated on industrial and software vulnerabilities. CISA advisories name Dorsett Controls InfoScan and several Siemens products, while the available snippets describe only fragments of the issues. One reports that successful exploitation of vulnerabilities could allow sensitive information retrieval; others mention MCP Server vulnerabilities, command injection, active content execution, and authentication bypass.

The KEV Catalog item adds a distinct signal: CISA says one vulnerability was added based on evidence of active exploitation. The snippet does not identify that vulnerability, so it cannot be matched here to the other advisories. Together, the stories suggest defenders should distinguish product-specific advisory details from the separate catalog notice, then establish which systems and versions are present.

For analysts, the limited descriptions make the linked advisories and affected-product inventories important next checks. Confirming applicability before drawing connections may help avoid treating these reports as one incident or vulnerability set. Watch for fuller advisory details, remediation guidance, and whether the catalog entry can be mapped to systems in your environment.
takeaways: Inventory industrial software to establish whether the named products are present.
Review the KEV Catalog entry separately from the product advisories.
Use full advisory details to confirm applicability and mitigation steps.
